title: Osiris myth as preserving antediluvian knowledge via Byblos
summary: Tim Alberino tells of Osiris myth as preserving antediluvian knowledge via Byblos, about post-flood antiquity at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: So what we have essentially here is an ark floating on the water with a body of knowledge inside of it from the anti-dolivian world.

plain: Tim Alberino, a guest on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, reads the ancient Egyptian myth of the god Osiris, whose story links Egypt with Byblos, an old port city on the Phoenician coast, as a hidden record. He says the myth is essentially about an ark floating on the water carrying a body of knowledge from the world before the great flood. If true, it would mean the myth preserves knowledge from a lost civilisation.
